text:
Mastering Data Storytelling with the Right Charts in Power BI 🌈...

One of the biggest mistakes I see in reporting and dashboards is not wrong data, but wrong visualization.

The chart you choose can make or break your audience's understanding of the insights you want to share.

📊 Data Storytelling is not just about visuals - it's about clarity, context, and impact.

👉🏻 Here's how to choose the right chart in Power BI (or any BI tool):

🔹1. Bar Chart - Compare values across categories

🔹2. Line Chart - Show trends over time✓

🔹3. Pie/Donut Chart - Highlight proportions in a whole

🔹4. Scatter Plot - Spot relationships & clusters

🔹5. Histogram - Analyze frequency distribution

🔹6. Radar Chart - Compare multi-dimensional data

🔹7. Heat Map - Highlight intensity & density

🔹8. Bubble Chart - Display 3-variable relationships

🔹9. Map Chart - Represent geo-tied data

✅Always ask: What story am I telling, and what decision should this enable?

By mastering chart selection, you turn dashboards into decision-driving tools.

author: Harsh Gupta
headline: Data Analyst 2 @ Brightly Software | Power BI, Snowflake
text:
The “Simple” SQL Question That Stumps Everyone 
In my PwC interview, they asked:
👉 “Find the 2nd highest salary from the Employee table.”

I smiled — “Easy!” I thought.
But then came the trap… they asked: “Can you show me another way?”
…and then another.

That’s when I realized: this single question can expose how deep your SQL knowledge really is.

Here are 5 ways to solve it 👇

🧩 Problem Setup

Table: Employee

ID | Name | Salary
-------------------
1 | A | 5000
2 | B | 7000
3 | C | 6000
4 | D | 7000
5 | E | 8000

We need the 2nd highest salary = 7000.


🔑 5 Solutions

1️⃣ Subquery with MAX

SELECT MAX(Salary) 
FROM Employee
WHERE Salary < (SELECT MAX(Salary) FROM Employee);

2️⃣ ORDER BY + LIMIT (MySQL)

SELECT Salary 
FROM Employee
ORDER BY Salary DESC
LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;

3️⃣ RANK() Window Function

SELECT Salary
FROM (
 SELECT Salary, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS rnk
 FROM Employee
) t
WHERE rnk = 2;

4️⃣ DENSE_RANK() for duplicates

SELECT Salary
FROM (
 SELECT Salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS drnk
 FROM Employee
) t
WHERE drnk = 2;

5️⃣ CTE with NOT IN

WITH cte AS (
 SELECT MAX(Salary) AS max_sal FROM Employee
)
SELECT MAX(Salary)
FROM Employee
WHERE Salary NOT IN (SELECT max_sal FROM cte);

💡 Why this matters:

Recruiters don’t just check if you know SQL.

They test if you can solve the same problem in multiple ways.

This shows adaptability — a skill every data role needs.

text:
Fine-tuning massive LLMs used to be painfully slow, but not anymore!

4 open source libraries that accelerate fine-tuning of Large Language Models

1. Unsloth AI

• Fine-tune models like Qwen3, Llama 4, and Gemma 3 up to 2× faster with 70% less VRAM
• Uses optimized Triton kernels and manual backprop for exact accuracy
• Supports low-resource setups and runs on consumer GPUs or even Colab/Kaggle with ~3 GB VRAM

GitHub repo → https://lnkd.in/g4MfgVh3

2. LLaMA Factory

• Fine-tune over 100 models (LLaMA, Mistral, Gemma, etc.) using a simple CLI or WebUI
• Supports LoRA, QLoRA, full or frozen fine-tuning across 2–8‑bit precision
• Includes built-in dataset templates, training monitors, and model export options

GitHub repo → https://lnkd.in/gTpaFzY2

3. DeepSpeed

• Built for large-scale distributed fine-tuning with ZeRO and FSDP
• Optimized for multi-GPU and multi-node training with advanced memory management
• Trusted in production environments for scalable LLM training

GitHub repo → https://lnkd.in/gUpE66zw

4. Axolotl

• Yaml-based setup for fine-tuning, LoRA/QLoRA, DPO, GRPO, and multimodal workflows
• Includes kernel optimizations for memory-efficient training
• Actively maintained with support for Hugging Face, model export, and inference

GitHub repo → https://lnkd.in/giRYvhsc

If there’s any other library you think should be in the list, drop them in the comments!
